subtype: Approach: telling the teacher when the friend will not stop [Revision]
passage: I am Shreya, and on Monday I saw Kabir on the stairs looking as if he had swallowed a stone. He had said no to his friend Salma twice about copying in the annual exam, and then he heard that Salma planned to bring a chit inside a pencil box. At break he walked to the staffroom door and asked his teacher Ms Iyer if he could talk to her alone. He was in there for five minutes. When he came out his face was red, and he said only, "I am not sure that was right, but it would have been worse." I do not know how he feels about Salma now, and I did not ask.

qa.q: Where did Salma plan to hide the chit?
qa.a: Salma planned to bring it inside a pencil box.

qa.q: How did Kabir seem to feel after speaking to Ms Iyer?
qa.a: Uneasy but resolved, since his face was red and he said he was not sure it was right but that it would have been worse.

qa.q: What other step could Kabir add for his friendship with Salma?
qa.a: He could tell Salma honestly why he spoke up and offer to help Salma study, because it shows he acted out of concern.

qa.q: How might Ms Iyer see Kabir coming to her?
qa.a: As a serious step, since he asked to talk alone and stayed five minutes, and she can now deal with a problem before the exam.

grounding: After refusing twice, a boy learns the friend plans a chit and tells the teacher privately, judging it worth stopping the bigger problem.
